📌 New York, IRNA – Russia and China have vetoed an anti-Iran US draft resolution at the United Nations Security Council aimed at extending the mandate of the Expert Panel of the 1737 Committee.

In the meeting, held under the agenda “Non-Proliferation” regarding the activities of the 1737 Sanctions Committee regarding Iran, the United States presented a draft resolution to the UN Security Council to extend the mandate of the 1737 Committee’s Panel of Experts (PoE).
​
Russia and China voted against, Somalia and Pakistan abstained, and the other 11 members of the Council voted in favor of the US draft resolution.
​
The adoption of a draft resolution in the UN Security Council requires at least nine votes without a veto from any of the 15 members. Although the US draft received 11 positive votes, it was vetoed by Russia and China and was therefore not adopted.

Chokh Terraces, Russia

High in the mountains of Dagestan, where the wind whispers tales older than memory, the Chokh Terraces rise — a stunning cascade of green steps sculpted into the rugged slopes.

These ancient agricultural terraces encircle the village of Chokh, one of the oldest settlements in the Caucasus. Tier upon tier, they unfold like a natural amphitheater, each level echoing centuries of resilience, tradition, and deep connection to the land.

From above, they resemble a living painting. Up close, they reveal a quiet rhythm — stone pathways winding through pastures, grazing sheep, and the gentle hush of mountain air.

The Chokh Terraces are more than a landscape. They’re a legacy — rooted in the earth, reaching toward the sky.
